messages:
alana: Heads-up — we have an edge case on a DSAR erasure. User requested deletion 2026-03-18, erasure-orch reported success (job 342) but today some embeddings resurfaced in the search index after an automated snapshot restore. Can we triage whether this is an orchestration rollback, backup restore, or KMS/RBAC cause?

matt: Ugh. Which region/account? service names?

alana: eu-west1 tenant acct-492. Services involved: erasure-orch (k8s job), snapshot-cleaner (periodic), and redis-cache-indexer. Snapshot restore came from long-term backups (daily-archive). Not sure which actor triggered it.

sia: @alana first things to check: audit log for snapshot restore events, KMS key access logs around the restore time, and the erasure-orch job logs to confirm tombstone marks. If the keystore rotated/loses decrypt perms, the cleaner sometimes skips delete and leaves a marker which later gets rehydrated by restore.

ezra-bot: alert: snapshot-cleaner triggered restore-of-archive id=arch-20260315-001 for acct-492 at 2026-03-20T11:42Z (automated lifecycle rule).

danielle (legal-ops): If user had a verified erasure request, we need to treat any reappearance as a legal incident. Please freeze any further restores for acct-492 and add the case id to audit events. I can open an incident if this is confirmed.

matt: Commands to grab logs:
```
# erasure job logs
kubectl -n infra logs job/erasure-orch-342 --since=72h | grep acct-492
# get admin activity for cloud snapshots
gcloud logging read 'resource.type=gce_snapshot AND protoPayload.request.resourceName:arch-20260315-001' --project=redwood-backups --freshness=72h
# KMS access
gcloud kms keys versions list --keyring=prod-keystore --key=acct-492-key --location=global --format=json
```
Use those and paste outputs here.

alana: grabbing logs now. One quick note — we rolled a small RBAC tweak to the dsar-erasure-service-account last week (removed editor, added custom role) — @matt can you check if that role still has 'cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.decrypt' on the backup key?

sia: If it doesn't, snapshot-cleaner may have skipped permanent delete and only marked as deleted in index. When lifecycle restore runs it will restore full state including the un-scrubbed blob.

matt: I see the RBAC change PR (internal/PR-4782). It granted kms.viewer but not cryptoKeyDecrypter. That would block decryption. Looks likely.

danielle (legal-ops): Please pause any automated restores until we verify. Also if this is an exception scenario we will want to log retention-exception=true on the case and notify privacy counsel.

alana: I'll pause snapshot lifecycle for acct-492 and add a temporary firewall rule to block snapshot restore jobs. Putting a note in the case.

matt: I'll open a quick RBAC rollback to re-add the decryption perm to dsar-erasure-service-account and run a dry-run erasure job against a staging snapshot.

sia: Also propose we add an audit annotation 'erasure-proof-id' to erasure-orch events and a finalizer that prevents restores until cleanup confirmed. This will help avoid rehydration loops.

danielle (legal-ops): Sounds good. Once paused, I'll coordinate the external DSAR notification if needed. Keep me posted before you re-enable restores.

alana: Taking ownership of remediation. ETA 2h to pause, collect logs, and file an incident if reappearance >1 item. @matt can you review the RBAC rollback?

matt: On it. Will ping when PR is up. :eyes:

sia: After fix we should run an end-to-end: 1) grant decrypter 2) run erasure-orch 3) verify tombstone+index scrub 4) run restore on a staging snapshot to confirm no rehydrate. I'll draft the checklist.

alana: Thanks team. Adding outputs here in a minute.
